children: GE Vernova's CEO expects the power and grid equipment maker's backlog to reach $200 billion very early in 2027. GE Vernova
shares fell about 1.3% to $939.62 at 10.58am ET time on Thursday morning. The stock slipped even as management pointed to more orders ahead.

The company ended the second quarter with $176 billion in backlog. Reaching $200 billion would add $24 billion, or roughly 13.6%. Strong demand for turbines and grid equipment gives GE Vernova a long runway of work. Turning that work into revenue and service income is the next test.

The picture adds a check on the enthusiasm: GE Vernova's GF Score is just 23 out of 100, with financial strength standing out more than the other measures shown. A bigger order book could lift future earnings, but the company still has to deliver the equipment on time and protect its margins. Orders are promising. Profitable execution is what investors need to see.

title: GE Vernova Falls 1.3% as $200 Billion Backlog Test Approaches
